subject: physics
title: Weight, mass and gravitational field strength
key_idea: Weight is the force of gravity on an object. It depends on the mass of the object and the gravitational field strength where it is. Mass stays the same everywhere. Weight changes with the field strength.

blocks.text: Weight and mass are different quantities. This section covers what each one is and how weight is measured.

items.meaning: The amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg). It is a scalar.
The force acting on an object due to gravity, measured in newtons (N). It is a vector.
The force of gravity on each kilogram of mass at a point, in newtons per kilogram (N/kg).
The single point at which the weight of an object may be considered to act.

items: All matter has a gravitational field that attracts other matter.
The field strength is much greater for massive objects, such as a planet.
The force of gravity close to the Earth is due to the gravitational field around the Earth.
The weight of an object depends on the field strength at the point where the object is.
The weight of an object and its mass are directly proportional (W ∝ m).
Weight is measured with a calibrated spring-balance, called a newtonmeter.
The object hangs from the spring.
The spring stretches, and the scale shows the weight in newtons.
A mass is measured in kilograms, never in newtons.
Weight is a force in newtons. Mass is an amount of matter in kilograms.
Weight is directly proportional to mass.
Weight is measured with a newtonmeter.

diagram.question: A person has a mass of {m} kg. The gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the weight of the person.

items: W = m × g. Always give the unit, N for weight.
To find mass or g, rearrange the equation first.
Use the value of g that the question gives.

blocks.text: Gravitational field strength is different on different bodies in space. Mass does not change, so weight does.

items: A body with a larger field strength gives a larger weight for the same mass.
The Moon has a field strength of about 1.6 N/kg, so objects weigh less there than on Earth.
Mars is about 3.7 N/kg.
An astronaut has the greatest weight where g is largest, because W = m × g and the mass is fixed.

diagram.alt: Choose a mass and a body in space and see the weight.

blocks.text: Close to the Earth, an object falling freely has an acceleration of about 9.8 m/s². Some questions use 10 m/s², so it gains about 10 m/s of speed each second.

items: Mass is the same everywhere. Weight depends on g.
Weight is smaller on the Moon and larger on bodies with a bigger g.
Free fall near the Earth has an acceleration of about 9.8 m/s².

checks.q: Calculate the weight of a swimmer of mass 75 kg. Use g = 10 N/kg.
A student has a weight of 400 N. Calculate the mass of the student. Use g = 10 N/kg.
A rock has a mass of 6.0 kg on the Moon, where g = 1.6 N/kg. Calculate its weight and state the unit.

exam_phrases: weight depends on mass and gravitational field strength

mistakes.wrong: The rocket's weight decreased because the fuel is used.
mistakes.right: This only scores one mark if nothing else is credited. Say weight depends on mass and field strength, the mass decreases as fuel is burned (or g decreases), therefore the weight decreases.
The final answer must be given to 2 significant figures, so m = 72 kg.

worked_example.question: The engineer has a weight of 710 N. gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the mass of the engineer. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the substitution, the rearrangement, the unrounded value and the answer to 2 significant figures.

mistakes.wrong: g = 20 × 12 = 240 N/kg for a rock of weight 20 N and mass 12 kg.
mistakes.right: This scores one mark at most. Rearrange to g = W / m = 20 / 12 = 1.7 N/kg.
This is the inverse of the correct ratio. Weight goes on top: g = W / m.
The unit is a separate mark. Write 9.6 N or 9.6 newtons.

worked_example.question: A rock on the surface of the Earth has a mass of 12 kg. The weight of the same rock on the surface of the Moon is 20 N. Calculate the gravitational field strength on the surface of the Moon.
worked_example.tip: Rearrangement and substitution can come in either order. Answers that round to 1.7, such as 1.67, are accepted.

extra.heading: Why g differs from body to body

blocks.text: The field strength on the Moon is different from the Earth. The mark scheme looks for reasons linked to the two bodies.

items: The **mass** of the body is different.
The **radius** of the body is different.
The **density** of the body is different.

exam_phrases: recall weight = mass × gravitational field strength

mistakes.right: This is incorrect use of g and scores 1 mark. Rearrange to m = W / g = 4500 / 10 = 450 kg.

mistakes.wrong: The weight of the Rover on Mars is 693.75 N, which is the answer to 3 significant figures.
mistakes.right: 693.75 N is allowed for the calculation mark but gets no marks for significant figures. Round to 694 N.

mistakes.wrong: The weight of the Rover on Mars is 694.
mistakes.right: The unit is a mark. Write 694 N.

worked_example.question: The Mars Rover has a mass of 185 kg. The gravitational field strength (g) on Mars is 3.75 N/kg. Calculate the weight of the Rover vehicle on Mars. Show your working and give your answer to 3 significant figures. State the unit for weight.
answer_points: Recall: weight = mass × gravitational field strength.
Weight = 693.75, which is 694 to 3 significant figures (2 marks).
worked_example.tip: Two of the five marks are for rounding correctly to 3 significant figures, and one is for the unit.
